instructions:
Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 346 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

Draft:

Our principal wants every student to join at least one extracurricular activity. I understand why. Clubs and teams can be the best part of school. Still, I disagree with making them mandatory, because a requirement would hurt the students it is supposed to help and weaken the activities themselves.

First, many students simply do not have the time. My friend Marcus leaves school at 2:45 and is at his job at a grocery store by 3:30, four days a week. His paycheck helps his mother cover rent. Other students watch younger brothers and sisters until a parent gets home, or ride a bus that leaves right after the last bell and does not come back. For them, a required activity is not an opportunity. It is one more thing to fail at, and the punishment would land on the families with the least room in their schedules.

Second, forcing people into activities makes those activities worse. I played in the school band for two years, and the difference between someone who wanted to be there and someone whose parents made them sign up was obvious by the second rehearsal. The unwilling ones talked through practice and skipped concerts. Now imagine a yearbook staff or a soccer team where a third of the members joined only to meet a rule. The students who care would spend their energy dragging everyone else along.

Third, plenty of students already do worthwhile things that the school never sees. One girl in my class takes karate at a studio downtown. Another volunteers at her church's food pantry every Saturday. A rule that only counts school-sponsored activities tells them their commitments do not matter.

A better plan would be to make joining easier instead of mandatory. The school could hold an activity fair in September, run a late bus twice a week, and let some clubs meet during lunch. Students who join because they found something they like will stay, work hard, and bring their friends. Students who join because they were ordered to will count the days until they can quit.
